newsitem.title: CANADA: Methanex says costs higher than target.
newsitem.headline: Methanex says costs higher than target.

text.p: Methanex Corp, the world's biggest methanol producer, said Tuesday its costs were running about 10 percent above its targets but the company expressed confidence it would meet its cost-cutting goals by year end.
Methanex chief executive Pierre Choquette told analysts that the company's objective for 1997 was to reduce its delivered methanol cash cost to below US$100 a tonne.
"At this point in the first quarter, we are running about ten dollars per tonne above that objective....(But) this is not at all of concern to me," he said.

Choquette attributed the higher costs to strong natural gas prices in North America and Chile in the first quarter and higher transportation and delivery costs resulting from low inventories in the methanol market.
But he said gas prices were trending down and expressed confidence that the company would meet its objective.

"The key point I want to make is while we're above our target now, and above actually where we were last year, this is of no concern to me. I think the fundamentals are all as we want them and we will achieve by year end our targets on costs," he said.

Methanol is a chemical feedstock derived from natural gas. It is an ingredient in products ranging from paints, resins and building materials to gasoline additives, and demand has historically tracked the economic cycle.
Methanex earlier reported first quarter earnings of US$0.27 a share, up from US$0.08 a share a year earlier. This reflected record sales volumes and strong pricing for methanol, the company said.

Choquette said inventories were lean throughout the industry and at a bare-bones level of about 20 days supply at Methanex itself. The company would optimally like inventories to be around 30 to 35 days.
Sales volumes in the second quarter appeared to be approaching the first-quarter's level, he said.
The global price of methanol looks to be about US$200 a tonne currently, he said. The company reported a realized sales price of US$184 a tonne in the first quarter.
Methanex was able to pick up sales volume from some competitors who had supply problems in the first quarter, he said.
The company's new plant in Chile is performing well and exceeding its designed operating capacity by about 10 percent, Choquette said.
